assumptions.condition: The vectors \(W_1,\ldots,W_T\) are independent and identically distributed under \(P\).
Conditional on \(X_t\) and \(\mathcal F_{t-1}\), the action \(A_t\) is drawn from the logged distribution \(\pi_t(\cdot\mid X_t,\mathcal F_{t-1})\) independently of \((Y_t(a))_{a\in\mathcal A}\).
For every \(a\in\mathcal A\), \(x\in\mathcal X\), and \(\eta\in\mathsf H\), the policy satisfies \(\Pi(a\mid x,\eta)\ge\varepsilon\).
The common envelope satisfies \(\sup_{a\in\mathcal A,\theta\in\Theta}\|g(a,X_t,Y_t(a);\theta)\|_2\le B\) almost surely.
constants: \(B<\infty\), fixed across every horizon and member law

assumptions.condition: The map \(\theta\mapsto g(a,x,y;\theta)\) is continuously differentiable on a common open neighborhood of \(\operatorname{conv}(\Theta)\), with \(\|\partial_\theta g(a,x,y;\theta)\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le D_1\) there, and is twice continuously differentiable on the closed \(\rho\)-ball about \(\theta^*\), with \(\|\partial_\theta^2 g(a,x,y;\theta)\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le D_2\) throughout that ball.
constants: \(D_1,D_2<\infty\) and \(\rho>0\), fixed across every horizon and member law
\(\kappa(u)>0\) for every \(u>0\), fixed across every horizon and member law

standard.name: Uniform separation of a Z-functional root

constants: \(s_\Theta>0\), fixed across every horizon and member law
\(h_->0\), fixed across every horizon and member law

assumptions.condition: The common policy modulus satisfies \(\sup_{a\in\mathcal A,x\in\mathcal X}|\Pi(a\mid x,\eta)-\Pi(a\mid x,\eta')|\le L_\Pi\|\eta-\eta'\|_2\) for all \(\eta,\eta'\in\mathsf H\).
constants: \(L_\Pi<\infty\), fixed across every horizon and member law

assumptions.condition: There is an \(\mathsf H\)-valued random element \(\eta_\infty\) measurable with respect to \(\sigma(\bigcup_{t\ge1}\mathcal F_t)\).

novel.justification: This condition supplies only a terminally measurable state-space-valued representative. It imposes neither finite support nor pointwise convergence of the policy state; all approximation content is carried separately by the uniform Cesaro attraction modulus.

This single Cesaro inequality approximates the adaptive policy path by its terminal random representative. It is a falsifiable common-modulus class restriction and requires neither finite support nor pointwise state convergence.

assumptions.condition: The common deterministic error envelope satisfies \(e_T=T^{-1/2}+r_T+\delta_T\to0\).

novel.justification: The combined envelope is a proposal-specific class-level restriction coupling sampling fluctuation, Cesaro attraction error, and attraction-tail probability. It is directly satisfied by immediately locking finite-state adaptive rules and can be audited from replicated policy paths; Mourrat supplies only the martingale central-limit ingredient used after this envelope is imposed.

assumptions.condition: The terminal covariance satisfies \(\Omega_\infty\succeq\omega_-I_d\) almost surely.
constants: \(\omega_->0\), fixed across every horizon and member law

novel.justification: A common almost-sure lower eigenvalue bound for the terminal random covariance is the proposal-specific uniform variance-growth primitive. The matching upper bound is derived from policy-wide overlap and the bounded score, not assumed.

definitions.name: terminal-Cesaro-representative adaptive-experiment class
definitions.construction: For fixed \(\varepsilon,B,D_1,D_2,h_-,L_\Pi,\omega_-,\kappa,s_\Theta,\rho\) and common sequences \((r_T,\delta_T)_{T\ge1}\), define \(\mathfrak P_T=\{P:\text{at horizon }T,\ P\text{ satisfies every condition in }\mathrm{ass:iid\text{-}full\text{-}data},\ldots,\mathrm{ass:basin\text{-}nondegeneracy}\text{ with these same fixed envelopes and moduli}\}\). The random element \(\eta_\infty\) is only required to be terminally measurable and \(\mathsf H\)-valued. No finite support and no pointwise convergence of \(\eta_t\) to \(\eta_\infty\) are imposed; all path approximation is supplied by the uniform Cesaro inequality in \(\mathrm{ass:uniform\text{-}attraction\text{-}modulus}\).

definitions.name: adaptive IPW-Z estimator
definitions.construction: First choose a measurable preliminary estimator \(\widetilde\theta_T\in\Theta\) satisfying \(\|G_T(\widetilde\theta_T)\|_2\le\inf_{\theta\in\Theta}\|G_T(\theta)\|_2+T^{-1/2}(r_T+\delta_T)\), using a fixed measurable tie-breaking rule. Define the compact correspondence \(\mathcal Z_T=\{\theta\in\Theta:G_T(\theta)=0,\ \|\theta-\widetilde\theta_T\|_2\le\rho/2\}\) and \(E_T=\{\mathcal Z_T\ne\varnothing\}\). Continuity of \(G_T\) on compact \(\Theta\) makes \(\mathcal Z_T\) compact, and its standard joint measurability permits a fixed measurable lexicographic compact-set selector. On \(E_T\), let \(\widehat\theta_T\) be that selected member of \(\mathcal Z_T\); on \(E_T^c\), set \(\widehat\theta_T=\widetilde\theta_T\).

definitions.name: bounded two-state separation witness
definitions.construction: For every \(T\ge2\), let \(P^{\dagger}\) be the law with \(K=3\), \(d=2\), \(\Theta=[-1,1]^2\), \(\theta^*=0\), a singleton \(\mathcal X\), and constant \(X_t\). Independently across \(t\) and between arms, let \(Y_t(1)\) be equiprobable on \(\{-\sqrt{2/5},\sqrt{2/5}\}\), let \(Y_t(2)\) be equiprobable on \(\{-\sqrt{1/2},\sqrt{1/2}\}\), and set \(Y_t(3)=0\). Set \(g(1,x,y;\theta)=(y-\theta_1,0)^\top\), \(g(2,x,y;\theta)=(0,y-\theta_2)^\top\), and \(g(3,x,y;\theta)=0\). Take \(m=2\), \(q=1\), \(\mathsf H=[0,1]\), \(\bar\eta_1=0\), \(\bar\eta_2=1\), and linearly interpolate the context-free policy between \(\Pi(\cdot\mid x,0)=(2/5,1/4,7/20)\) and \(\Pi(\cdot\mid x,1)=(2/5,1/6,13/30)\). Start at \(\eta_0=1/2\), set \(J=1\) if and only if \(A_1=1\), set \(J=2\) otherwise, define \(\eta_\infty=\bar\eta_J=J-1\), and put \(\eta_t=\eta_\infty\) for every \(t\ge1\).

definitions.name: terminal-representative covariance
definitions.construction:
For \(\eta\in\mathsf H\), define
\[
 \Gamma_P(\eta)=E_P\!\left[\sum_{a\in\mathcal A}
 \frac{g(a,X_t,Y_t(a);\theta^*)g(a,X_t,Y_t(a);\theta^*)^\top}
 {\Pi(a\mid X_t,\eta)}\right].
\]
Set \(\Omega_\infty=\Gamma_P(\eta_\infty)\) and \(V_\infty=H^{-1}\Omega_\infty H^{-\top}\). For any auxiliary finite-support representation \(\eta_\infty=\bar\eta_J\) almost surely with \(\mathcal J=\{j:P(J=j)>0\}\), set \(p_j=P(J=j)\), \(\Omega_j=\Gamma_P(\bar\eta_j)\), \(V_j=H^{-1}\Omega_jH^{-\top}\), \(\Omega_J=\sum_{j\in\mathcal J}\mathbf 1\{J=j\}\Omega_j\), and \(V_J=\sum_{j\in\mathcal J}\mathbf 1\{J=j\}V_j\). These finite-support objects are auxiliary specializations and are not restrictions on the class.

definitions.name: event-truncated realized-QV sandwich
definitions.construction: Set \(\widehat\Omega_T=T^{-1}\sum_{t=1}^T\widehat\xi_t\widehat\xi_t^\top\) and \(\mathcal E_T=\{\sigma_{\min}(\widehat H_T)\ge h_-/2,\ \lambda_{\min}(\widehat\Omega_T)\ge\omega_-/2\}\). Define \(\widehat V_T=\widehat H_T^{-1}\widehat\Omega_T\widehat H_T^{-\top}\) on \(\mathcal E_T\) and \(\widehat V_T=I_d\) on \(\mathcal E_T^c\).

definitions.name: bounded-noise Guo--Xu no-intercept recursion
definitions.construction: Fix \(K=2\), draw \(X_t\) independently and uniformly from \(\{-4,1\}\), and set \(Y_t(1)=1/2+\sigma_1R_{t,1}\) and \(Y_t(2)=1/12+\sigma_2R_{t,2}\), where the \(R_{t,a}\) are independent centered Rademacher innovations and \(\sigma_1,\sigma_2>0\) are arbitrary fixed constants declared as part of this bounded analogue; no numerical innovation variances are attributed to Guo and Xu. Keep their no-intercept working model, ridge constant \(\lambda=1\), unit-precision ridge initialization, and updates \(\Phi^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,a}=\Phi^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t-1,a}+\mathbf 1\{A_t=a\}X_t^2\), \(b^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,a}=b^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t-1,a}+\mathbf 1\{A_t=a\}X_tY_t\), and \(\widehat\beta^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,a}=b^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,a}/\Phi^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,a}\). For \(\eta_0\in\mathsf K_{\mathrm{GX}}\), initialize \(Z^{\mathrm{GX}}_0=\iota_{\mathrm{GX}}(\eta_0)=(\eta_{0,1},\eta_{0,2},1,1)^\top\), equivalently \(\Phi^{\mathrm{GX}}_{0,a}=1\) and \(b^{\mathrm{GX}}_{0,a}=\eta_{0,a}\); the published initialization is the included case \(\eta_0=(0,0)^\top\). At occasion \(t\), break every exact index tie in favor of arm \(1\), maximize \(\widehat\beta^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t-1,a}X_t+|X_t|\sqrt{q^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t-1,a}}\), and then assign the maximizing arm with probability \(0.99\) and the other arm with probability \(0.01\). The process of interest is the slope projection \((\widehat\beta^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,1},\widehat\beta^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,2})^\top\) of \(Z^{\mathrm{GX}}_t\), not a slope-only Markov chain.

definitions.name: bounded-recursion dynamics certification handle
definitions.construction: Write \(Z^{\mathrm{GX}}_t=(\beta_1,\beta_2,q_1,q_2)^\top\) for a current augmented state. Its induced armwise update is \(q_a^+=q_a/(1+\mathbf 1\{A=a\}q_aX^2)\) and \(\beta_a^+=(\beta_a+\mathbf 1\{A=a\}q_aXY(a))/(1+\mathbf 1\{A=a\}q_aX^2)\). The next clipped-UCB action uses \(\beta_aX+|X|\sqrt{q_a}\), so \(Z^{\mathrm{GX}}_t\), rather than its two-dimensional slope projection, is the time-homogeneous Markov state. For stochastic-approximation analysis, put \(D_{t,a}=\Phi^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,a}\), \(N_{t,a}=b^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,a}\), and, for \(t\ge1\), \(\Psi_t=(D_{t,1}/t,D_{t,2}/t,N_{t,1}/t,N_{t,2}/t)\). Analyze the exact \(1/(t+1)\) recursion for \(\Psi_t\) on an eventually compact region with both normalized Gram coordinates bounded away from zero. At the equal-slope surface, retain every limiting conditional-mean mode generated by the square-root UCB bonus: although the bonus is \(O(t^{-1/2})\), it can make the same arm greedy at both contexts inside an \(O(t^{-1/2})\) switching layer. Thus a closed convexified limiting graph must include these same-arm modes as well as the two opposite-context modes. Any differential-inclusion reduction must verify the closed-graph, compact-convex-value, boundedness, vanishing-perturbation, and martingale-tail conditions for this normalized recursion. Compact-uniform sequences \(r_T(K_0),\delta_T(K_0)\to0\) require a separate quantitative hitting or escape estimate and may not be inferred from pointwise convergence by a finite-cover argument.

statements.statement:
The common derivative and bounded-IPW envelopes imply
\[
 \|H\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le KD_1,
 \qquad \omega_-I_d\preceq\Omega_\infty\preceq(KB^2/\varepsilon)I_d
 \quad\text{almost surely}.
\]
There is a finite constant \(C\), independent of \(T\) and \(P\), such that
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathfrak P_T}E_P\!\left[\left\|T^{-1}\langle S\rangle_T-\Omega_\infty\right\|_{\mathrm{op}}\right]
 \le C(r_T+\delta_T).
\]
The preliminary estimator is uniformly consistent, \(G_T(\theta^*)=O_P(T^{-1/2})\), and \(\partial_\theta G_T(\theta^*)-H=O_P(T^{-1/2})\) uniformly. Together with \(D_2\rho/\varepsilon<h_-/4\), these bounds imply that, with probability tending uniformly to one, there is a unique empirical root in the closed \(\rho\)-ball about \(\theta^*\), it is \(O_P(T^{-1/2})\) from \(\theta^*\), and it is the unique member of \(\mathcal Z_T\). Hence \(\sup_{P\in\mathfrak P_T}P(E_T^c)\to0\), and
\[
 \sqrt T(\widehat\theta_T-\theta^*)+H^{-1}T^{-1/2}S_T=O_P(e_T)
\]
uniformly. The strongest terminal-representative-free distributional conclusion implied by these primitives is
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathfrak P_T}\sup_{\|c\|_2=1}\sup_{z\in\mathbb R}
 \left|P\left\{c^\top\sqrt T(\widehat\theta_T-\theta^*)\le z\right\}
 -E_P\Phi\left(\frac{z}{\sqrt{c^\top V_\infty c}}\right)\right|\longrightarrow0.
\]
Moreover,
\[
 \frac{\omega_-}{(KD_1)^2}I_d\preceq V_\infty
 \preceq\frac{KB^2}{\varepsilon h_-^2}I_d\quad\text{almost surely}.
\]
Thus, for every sequence \(P_T\in\mathfrak P_T\), the laws of \(V_\infty\) have a weakly convergent subsequence with a limiting law \(\mu\) supported on the displayed compact covariance set. Along that subsequence, every fixed nonzero contrast has the centered Gaussian scale-mixture limit \(\sqrt{c^\top Vc}\,Z_1\), where \(V\sim\mu\), \(Z_1\sim N(0,1)\), and \(V\) and \(Z_1\) are independent. This limit is Gaussian if and only if \(c^\top Vc\) is \(\mu\)-almost surely constant. In general, the class primitives do not imply stable convergence relative to \(\sigma(\eta_\infty)\), even when \(V_\infty\) is deterministic.
statements.justification: This theorem derives predictable-QV control, exact-root localization, and the maximal terminal-representative-free Gaussian scale-mixture approximation without imposing finite covariance support.

statements.proof_tex:
Write \(g_{t,a}(\theta)=g(a,X_t,Y_t(a);\theta)\). By sequential randomization, conditional independence of the action and current potential outcomes, i.i.d. full-data arrivals, and the overlap bound that makes every denominator positive,
\[
\begin{aligned}
 E_P[\xi_t\mid\mathcal F_{t-1}]
 &=E_P\!\left[E_P\!\left\{\left.\sum_{a\in\mathcal A}
 \frac{\mathbf 1\{A_t=a\}g_{t,a}(\theta^*)}
 {\pi_t(a\mid X_t,\mathcal F_{t-1})}\right|W_t,\mathcal F_{t-1}\right\}\middle|\mathcal F_{t-1}\right]\\
 &=E_P\!\left[\sum_{a\in\mathcal A}g_{t,a}(\theta^*)\right]
 =M_P(\theta^*)=0.
\end{aligned}\tag{1}
\]
Thus \((\xi_t,\mathcal F_t)\) is a martingale-difference array. The same conditioning calculation and \(\mathrm{def:basin\text{-}covariance}\) give
\[
 E_P[\xi_t\xi_t^\top\mid\mathcal F_{t-1}]
 =\Gamma_P(\eta_{t-1}),
 \qquad \Omega_\infty=\Gamma_P(\eta_\infty). \tag{2}
\]
The bounded-score and overlap assumptions imply \(\|\xi_t\|_2\le B/\varepsilon\). For every unit vector \(u\),
\[
 u^\top\Gamma_P(\eta)u
 \le E_P\!\left[\sum_{a\in\mathcal A}
 \frac{\|g_{t,a}(\theta^*)\|_2^2}{\Pi(a\mid X_t,\eta)}\right]
 \le\frac{KB^2}{\varepsilon}. \tag{3}
\]
Consequently \(\Omega_\infty\preceq(KB^2/\varepsilon)I_d\), while \(\Omega_\infty\succeq\omega_-I_d\) is the basin-nondegeneracy assumption. The derivative envelope permits differentiation through the finite sum and expectation and yields
\[
 \|H\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 \le E_P\!\left[\sum_{a\in\mathcal A}
 \|\partial_\theta g_{t,a}(\theta^*)\|_{\mathrm{op}}\right]
 \le KD_1. \tag{4}
\]

For \(p,q\ge\varepsilon\), \(|p^{-1}-q^{-1}|\le|p-q|/\varepsilon^2\). The policy-Lipschitz assumption and the definition of \(\Gamma_P\) therefore give
\[
 \|\Gamma_P(\eta)-\Gamma_P(\eta')\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 \le L_\Gamma\|\eta-\eta'\|_2,
 \qquad L_\Gamma=\frac{KB^2L_\Pi}{\varepsilon^2}, \tag{5}
\]
and \(\|\Gamma_P(\eta)\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le M_\Gamma:=KB^2/\varepsilon\). On
\[
 \mathcal A_T=\left\{T^{-1}\sum_{t=1}^T
 \|\eta_{t-1}-\eta_\infty\|_2\le r_T\right\},
\]
equations (2) and (5) imply
\[
 \left\|T^{-1}\langle S\rangle_T-\Omega_\infty\right\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 \le L_\Gamma r_T. \tag{6}
\]
On \(\mathcal A_T^c\) the norm is at most \(2M_\Gamma\), and the uniform-attraction assumption gives \(P(\mathcal A_T^c)\le\delta_T\). Hence
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathfrak P_T}E_P\left\|T^{-1}\langle S\rangle_T-\Omega_\infty\right\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 \le L_\Gamma r_T+2M_\Gamma\delta_T
 \le C(r_T+\delta_T). \tag{7}
\]

We next derive localization. For fixed \(\theta\), sequential randomization and i.i.d. arrivals show that the summands of \(G_T(\theta)-M_P(\theta)\) are mean-zero martingale differences. Their norms are uniformly bounded, so martingale orthogonality gives
\[
 E_P\|G_T(\theta)-M_P(\theta)\|_2^2\le C_0/T. \tag{8}
\]
The empirical and population maps are uniformly Lipschitz in \(\theta\), with respective moduli \(D_1/\varepsilon\) and \(KD_1\). For fixed \(x>0\), cover compact \(\Theta\) by a finite mesh fine enough that the two Lipschitz approximation errors total at most \(x/2\). Chebyshev's inequality applied to (8) and a union bound prove
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathfrak P_T}P\left\{\sup_{\theta\in\Theta}
 \|G_T(\theta)-M_P(\theta)\|_2>x\right\}\longrightarrow0. \tag{9}
\]
Since \(M_P(\theta^*)=0\) and the preliminary estimator satisfies its defining approximate-minimum inequality,
\[
 \|M_P(\widetilde\theta_T)\|_2
 \le2\sup_{\theta\in\Theta}\|G_T(\theta)-M_P(\theta)\|_2
 +T^{-1/2}(r_T+\delta_T)=o_P(1) \tag{10}
\]
uniformly. Root separation therefore yields, for every \(u>0\),
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathfrak P_T}P\{\|\widetilde\theta_T-\theta^*\|_2\ge u\}
 \le\sup_{P\in\mathfrak P_T}P\{\|M_P(\widetilde\theta_T)\|_2\ge\kappa(u)\}
 \longrightarrow0. \tag{11}
\]

At \(\theta^*\), \(G_T(\theta^*)=S_T/T\), so (1), martingale orthogonality, and bounded increments imply \(G_T(\theta^*)=O_P(T^{-1/2})\) uniformly. Applying the same entrywise argument to the derivative score gives
\[
 R_T:=\partial_\theta G_T(\theta^*)-H=O_P(T^{-1/2}) \tag{12}
\]
uniformly. On the closed \(\rho\)-ball about \(\theta^*\), the curvature and overlap bounds imply
\[
 \sup_{\|\theta-\theta^*\|_2\le\rho}
 \|\partial_\theta G_T(\theta)-H\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 \le\|R_T\|_{\mathrm{op}}+D_2\rho/\varepsilon. \tag{13}
\]
The radius restriction, (12), and \(\sigma_{\min}(H)\ge h_-\) make the right side smaller than \(h_-/2\) with probability tending uniformly to one. On that event set \(\Psi_T(\theta)=\theta-H^{-1}G_T(\theta)\). Equation (13) and \(\|H^{-1}\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le h_-^{-1}\) show that \(\Psi_T\) is a contraction with modulus at most \(1/2\) on the ball, and
\[
 \|\Psi_T(\theta)-\theta^*\|_2
 \le\tfrac12\|\theta-\theta^*\|_2+h_-^{-1}\|G_T(\theta^*)\|_2. \tag{14}
\]
The last term is at most \(\rho/2\) with probability tending uniformly to one, and root interiority puts the closed ball inside \(\Theta\). Iteration from any point in the ball produces a Cauchy sequence whose limit \(\theta_T^0\) is the unique fixed point, hence the unique empirical root, in that ball. Moreover,
\[
 \|\theta_T^0-\theta^*\|_2
 \le2h_-^{-1}\|G_T(\theta^*)\|_2=O_P(T^{-1/2}). \tag{15}
\]
Equations (11) and (15) put both \(\widetilde\theta_T\) and \(\theta_T^0\) within \(\rho/4\) of \(\theta^*\) with probability tending uniformly to one. Then \(\theta_T^0\in\mathcal Z_T\), while every member of \(\mathcal Z_T\) is within \(3\rho/4\) of \(\theta^*\) and must equal the unique root \(\theta_T^0\). Thus
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathfrak P_T}P(E_T^c)\to0,
 \qquad \widehat\theta_T=\theta_T^0
\]
outside a uniformly negligible event.

Put \(\Delta_T=\widehat\theta_T-\theta^*\). On the exact-root event, Taylor's formula and the curvature bound give
\[
 0=G_T(\widehat\theta_T)
 =T^{-1}S_T+H\Delta_T+R_T\Delta_T+R_T^{(2)},
 \qquad \|R_T^{(2)}\|_2\le\frac{D_2}{2\varepsilon}\|\Delta_T\|_2^2. \tag{16}
\]
Using (12), (15), and \(\|H^{-1}\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le h_-^{-1}\) in (16) yields
\[
 \sqrt T\Delta_T+H^{-1}T^{-1/2}S_T
 =O_P(T^{-1/2})=O_P(e_T). \tag{17}
\]
The fallback branch is uniformly negligible, so (17) holds unconditionally in the uniform-in-probability sense.

It remains to derive the terminal-representative-free mixture approximation. Let
\[
 \beta_T=\max\{T^{-1/2},\sqrt{r_T}\},\qquad
 k_T=\lceil T\beta_T\rceil,\qquad
 \Lambda_T=k_T^{-1}\sum_{t=1}^{k_T}\Gamma_P(\eta_{t-1}). \tag{18}
\]
The vanishing-modulus assumption gives \(k_T/T\to0\) and \(Tr_T/k_T\le\sqrt{r_T}+o(1)\). The matrix \(\Lambda_T\) is \(\mathcal F_{k_T}\)-measurable. Repeating (6)--(7), first on the prefix and then on the suffix, gives
\[
 E_P\|\Lambda_T-\Omega_\infty\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 \le L_\Gamma\frac{Tr_T}{k_T}+2M_\Gamma\delta_T=o(1), \tag{19}
\]
uniformly, and, for \(B_T=T^{-1}\sum_{t=k_T+1}^T\Gamma_P(\eta_{t-1})\),
\[
 E_P\|B_T-\Omega_\infty\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 \le L_\Gamma r_T+M_\Gamma k_T/T+2M_\Gamma\delta_T=o(1). \tag{20}
\]
Thus \(E_P\|B_T-\Lambda_T\|_{\mathrm{op}}=o(1)\) uniformly.

Fix a unit vector \(c\) and set \(a=H^{-\top}c\). Equations (4) and the Jacobian lower bound imply
\[
 (KD_1)^{-1}\le\|a\|_2\le h_-^{-1}. \tag{21}
\]
Therefore \(|a^\top\xi_t|\le B/(\varepsilon h_-)\), while nondegeneracy gives
\[
 a^\top\Omega_\infty a\ge v_0:=\frac{\omega_-}{(KD_1)^2}>0. \tag{22}
\]
Define the \(\mathcal F_{k_T}\)-measurable clipped variance
\[
 \lambda_{T,P,c}=\max\{v_0/2,a^\top\Lambda_Ta\}. \tag{23}
\]
It lies between \(v_0/2\) and a common finite upper bound. Since clipping is one-Lipschitz and fixes every number at least \(v_0\), (19)--(22) give
\[
 E_P|a^\top B_Ta-\lambda_{T,P,c}|=o(1),
 \qquad E_P|a^\top\Omega_\infty a-\lambda_{T,P,c}|=o(1) \tag{24}
\]
uniformly in \(P\) and unit \(c\).

Apply \(\mathrm{lem:early\text{-}measurable\text{-}martingale\text{-}mixture}\) to \(X_{T,t}=-a^\top\xi_t\), \(\mathcal G_{T,t}=\mathcal F_t\), and (23). Its martingale-difference, bounded-increment, early-measurability, positive-variance, and quadratic-variation hypotheses are respectively (1), (21), (23), (22)--(23), and the first part of (24). Hence
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathfrak P_T}\sup_{\|c\|_2=1}\sup_{z\in\mathbb R}
 \left|P\left\{-a^\top T^{-1/2}\sum_{t=k_T+1}^T\xi_t\le z\right\}
 -E_P\Phi\left(\frac z{\sqrt{\lambda_{T,P,c}}}\right)\right|\to0. \tag{25}
\]
Let \(\phi\) denote the standard normal density. For variances in a fixed compact interval bounded away from zero,
\[
 \sup_z\left|\frac{\partial}{\partial v}\Phi(z/\sqrt v)\right|
 =\sup_x\frac{|x|\phi(x)}{2v}\le C/v_0. \tag{26}
\]
The second part of (24) and (26) replace the expectation in (25) by
\[
 E_P\Phi\left(\frac z{\sqrt{a^\top\Omega_\infty a}}\right)
 =E_P\Phi\left(\frac z{\sqrt{c^\top V_\infty c}}\right). \tag{27}
\]
Martingale orthogonality and bounded increments give
\[
 E_P\left|a^\top T^{-1/2}\sum_{t=1}^{k_T}\xi_t\right|^2
 \le Ck_T/T=o(1). \tag{28}
\]
The exact-root remainder in (17) is also uniformly negligible. The mixture distributions in (27) have densities uniformly bounded by (22). The inclusions
\[
 \{X+R\le z\}\subseteq\{X\le z+\eta\}\cup\{|R|>\eta\},
 \qquad
 \{X\le z-\eta\}\subseteq\{X+R\le z\}\cup\{|R|>\eta\}
\]
then transfer (25)--(28) through both remainders, first letting \(T\to\infty\) and then \(\eta\downarrow0\). This proves the uniform mixture approximation.

For every unit \(u\),
\[
 u^\top V_\infty u=(H^{-\top}u)^\top\Omega_\infty(H^{-\top}u).
\]
The upper bounds in (3) and \(\|H^{-1}\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le h_-^{-1}\), and the lower bounds in (4) and \(\Omega_\infty\succeq\omega_-I_d\), imply
\[
 \frac{\omega_-}{(KD_1)^2}I_d\preceq V_\infty
 \preceq\frac{KB^2}{\varepsilon h_-^2}I_d. \tag{29}
\]
Apply \(\mathrm{lem:compact\text{-}covariance\text{-}law\text{-}subsequence}\) to the laws of \(V_\infty\) along any triangular sequence \(P_T\). It gives a subsequence and weak limit \(\mu\). For fixed nonzero \(c\) and every \(z\), the map
\[
 v\longmapsto\Phi\left(z/\sqrt{c^\top vc}\right)
\]
is bounded and continuous on the compact set in (29); hence the uniform mixture approximation converges to \(\int\Phi(z/\sqrt{c^\top vc})\,d\mu(v)\). This is the law of \(X=\sqrt{c^\top Vc}\,Z_1\) for independent \(V\sim\mu\) and \(Z_1\sim N(0,1)\).

Put \(Q=c^\top Vc\). The bounds in (29) make its first two moments finite and positive. Independence gives
\[
 E[X^2]=E[Q],\qquad E[X^4]=3E[Q^2]. \tag{30}
\]
If \(Q=q\) almost surely, then \(X\sim N(0,q)\). Conversely, if \(X\) is centered Gaussian, its variance must be \(E[Q]\), and its fourth moment is \(3(E[Q])^2\). Equation (30) then gives \(\operatorname{Var}(Q)=0\). Thus the limit is Gaussian exactly when its projected variance mixing law is degenerate.

Finally, stable convergence relative to the terminal representative is not implied. For odd \(T\), take \(d=1\), two actions with constant probabilities \((1/2,1/2)\), i.i.d. Rademacher variables \(R_t\), \(Y_t(1)=Y_t(2)=R_t\), and \(g(a,x,y;\theta)=(y-\theta)/2\) on \(\Theta=[-1,1]\). Let \(\mathsf H=[-1,1]\), set every predictable state \(\eta_t=0\), take \(r_T=T^{-1/4}\), \(\delta_T=0\), and define the terminally measurable representative
\[
 \eta_\infty=r_T\,\operatorname{sgn}\left(\sum_{t=1}^TR_t\right). \tag{31}
\]
Then the attraction average is exactly \(r_T\). The policy is constant in its state, so \(\Omega_\infty=V_\infty=1\). All remaining primitives hold with fixed envelopes: \(M_P(\theta)=-\theta\), \(H=-1\), and the exact empirical root is \(T^{-1}\sum_tR_t\). Indeed, the full-data vectors are i.i.d.; constant half--half assignment is sequentially randomized and has any fixed overlap floor \(\varepsilon<1/2\); the score and its first derivative are bounded by one, while its second derivative is zero; \(\kappa(u)=u\), \(s_\Theta=1\), and \(h_-=1\) are valid; the constant policy has every positive Lipschitz envelope; and \(\Omega_\infty=1\) permits \(\omega_-=1\). Taking any fixed \(D_2>0\) and \(0<\rho<\min\{1,\varepsilon/(4D_2)\}\) satisfies the radius condition. Finally, \(e_T=T^{-1/2}+T^{-1/4}\to0\). Thus this is a genuine triangular sequence in one fixed-envelope class.

Let \(h_T=\operatorname{sgn}(\eta_\infty)\) and \(f(x)=\tanh(x)\). Symmetry gives \(E[h_T]=0\), whereas
\[
 E\left[h_Tf\left(T^{-1/2}\sum_{t=1}^TR_t\right)\right]
 =E\left|\tanh\left(T^{-1/2}\sum_{t=1}^TR_t\right)\right|. \tag{32}
\]
This is bounded away from zero. Indeed, for \(X_T=T^{-1}(\sum_tR_t)^2\), independence gives \(E[X_T]=1\) and \(E[X_T^2]=3-2/T\le3\). If \(A_T=\{X_T>1/2\}\), then
\[
 1=E[X_T]\le\tfrac12+E[X_T\mathbf1_{A_T}]
 \le\tfrac12+\sqrt{3P(A_T)},
\]
so \(P(A_T)\ge1/12\), and (32) is at least \(\tanh(1/\sqrt2)/12\). Uniform stable convergence to a Gaussian innovation independent of \(\sigma(\eta_\infty)\) would instead force (32) to converge to \(E[h_T]E[f(Z_1)]=0\). This contradiction proves the final assertion while leaving the marginal scale-mixture approximation intact.

Using the exact-root linearization on \(E_T\) and carrying its uniformly negligible fallback event \(E_T^c\), uniformly over \(P\in\mathfrak P_T\),
\[
 T^{-1}([S]_T-\langle S\rangle_T)=O_P(T^{-1/2}),\qquad
 \widehat\Omega_T-\Omega_\infty=O_P(e_T),\qquad
 \widehat H_T-H=O_P(e_T).
\]
Consequently \(\sup_{P\in\mathfrak P_T}P(\mathcal E_T^c)\to0\), the event truncation is asymptotically inactive uniformly, and \(\widehat V_T-V_\infty=O_P(e_T)\). Moreover,
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathfrak P_T}\sup_{\|c\|_2=1}\sup_{z\in\mathbb R}
 \left|P\{T_T^{\mathrm{rqv}}(c)\le z\}-\Phi(z)\right|\longrightarrow0.
\]
For the realized-QV interval \(I_T^{\mathrm{rqv}}(c,\alpha)\) in \(\mathrm{def:realized\text{-}qv\text{-}wald\text{-}interval}\), every fixed \(\alpha\in(0,1)\) satisfies
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathfrak P_T}\sup_{\|c\|_2=1}
 \left|P\{\tau\in I_T^{\mathrm{rqv}}(c,\alpha)\}-(1-\alpha)\right|\longrightarrow0.
\]
This derives the self-normalized variance-ratio, invertibility-event, and inverse-QV controls from the terminal-representative Cesaro attraction and exact-root localization primitives. The class and estimator are neither a subclass nor a superclass of Saco's published pointwise AIPW/DML setup as stated.
statements.justification: The always-defined truncated sandwich tracks the arbitrary terminal covariance, becomes asymptotically untruncated uniformly, and removes even a continuously mixed Gaussian scale without estimating its mixing law.
statements.gap: Saco proves a pointwise self-normalized result for a distinct AIPW/DML setup. This theorem verifies variance growth, realized-to-predictable QV, exact-root, feasible-inverse, and truncation controls uniformly for the present bounded IPW-Z terminal-representative class; neither published class contains the other as stated.
statements.consumer: The theorem gives a feasible standard-normal Wald interval for HeartSteps-style causal excursion contrasts under path-dependent adaptive assignment.
statements.proof_tex:
All stochastic orders below are uniform over \(P\in\mathfrak P_T\) and, when present, over \(\|c\|_2=1\). Bounded scores and overlap give
\[
 \|\xi_t\|_2\le M_\xi:=B/\varepsilon. \tag{1}
\]
Define \(D_t=\xi_t\xi_t^\top-E_P[\xi_t\xi_t^\top\mid\mathcal F_{t-1}]\). Every entry of \(D_t\) is a martingale difference and \(\|D_t\|_{\mathrm F}\le2M_\xi^2\). Orthogonality over the fixed \(d^2\) entries yields
\[
 E_P\left\|T^{-1}\sum_{t=1}^TD_t\right\|_{\mathrm F}^2
 =T^{-2}\sum_{t=1}^TE_P\|D_t\|_{\mathrm F}^2
 \le\frac{4M_\xi^4}{T}. \tag{2}
\]
Since operator norm is bounded by Frobenius norm, Chebyshev's inequality gives
\[
 T^{-1}([S]_T-\langle S\rangle_T)=O_P(T^{-1/2}). \tag{3}
\]

Theorem \(\mathrm{thm:basin\text{-}stable\text{-}ipwz}\) gives
\[
 \|\widehat\theta_T-\theta^*\|_2=O_P(T^{-1/2}),
 \qquad \partial_\theta G_T(\theta^*)-H=O_P(T^{-1/2}). \tag{4}
\]
For every \(t\), the derivative and overlap bounds imply
\[
 \|\widehat\xi_t-\xi_t\|_2
 \le\frac{D_1}{\varepsilon}\|\widehat\theta_T-\theta^*\|_2. \tag{5}
\]
Both scores have norm at most \(M_\xi\), so
\[
 \|\widehat\xi_t\widehat\xi_t^\top-\xi_t\xi_t^\top\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 \le\frac{2BD_1}{\varepsilon^2}\|\widehat\theta_T-\theta^*\|_2. \tag{6}
\]
Averaging (6), then using (3)--(4), the predictable-QV expectation bound from the first theorem, and Markov's inequality, gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \|\widehat\Omega_T-\Omega_\infty\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 &\le\left\|T^{-1}\sum_{t=1}^T
 (\widehat\xi_t\widehat\xi_t^\top-\xi_t\xi_t^\top)\right\|_{\mathrm{op}}\\
 &\quad+\left\|T^{-1}([S]_T-\langle S\rangle_T)\right\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 +\left\|T^{-1}\langle S\rangle_T-\Omega_\infty\right\|_{\mathrm{op}}\\
 &=O_P(T^{-1/2}+r_T+\delta_T)=O_P(e_T).
\end{aligned}\tag{7}
\]
On the closed \(\rho\)-ball, curvature and overlap similarly imply, outside the negligible fallback event,
\[
 \|\widehat H_T-H\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 \le\|\partial_\theta G_T(\theta^*)-H\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 +\frac{D_2}{\varepsilon}\|\widehat\theta_T-\theta^*\|_2
 =O_P(T^{-1/2})=O_P(e_T). \tag{8}
\]
The fallback probability tends uniformly to zero, so (8) holds unconditionally in the uniform-in-probability sense.

The inequalities \(|\sigma_{\min}(A)-\sigma_{\min}(B)|\le\|A-B\|_{\mathrm{op}}\) and, for symmetric matrices, \(|\lambda_{\min}(A)-\lambda_{\min}(B)|\le\|A-B\|_{\mathrm{op}}\), follow from their variational definitions. Thus (7)--(8), \(\sigma_{\min}(H)\ge h_-\), and \(\Omega_\infty\succeq\omega_-I_d\) imply
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathfrak P_T}P(\mathcal E_T^c)\longrightarrow0. \tag{9}
\]
On \(\mathcal E_T\), every inverse is legally evaluated and
\[
 \widehat H_T^{-1}-H^{-1}
 =\widehat H_T^{-1}(H-\widehat H_T)H^{-1},
 \qquad \|\widehat H_T^{-1}\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le2/h_-. \tag{10}
\]
The first theorem also gives \(\|H^{-1}\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le h_-^{-1}\) and \(\|\Omega_\infty\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le KB^2/\varepsilon\). Inserting and subtracting the three sandwich factors one at a time and using (7)--(10) proves on \(\mathcal E_T\) that
\[
 \widehat H_T^{-1}\widehat\Omega_T\widehat H_T^{-\top}
 -H^{-1}\Omega_\infty H^{-\top}=O_P(e_T). \tag{11}
\]
On \(\mathcal E_T^c\), \(\widehat V_T=I_d\), while the first theorem bounds \(V_\infty\) uniformly. Equation (9) makes this branch negligible, so
\[
 \widehat V_T-V_\infty=O_P(e_T). \tag{12}
\]

Fix a unit vector \(c\), and define
\[
 a=H^{-\top}c,\qquad U_t=a^\top\xi_t,\qquad
 A_T^2=\sum_{t=1}^TE_P[U_t^2\mid\mathcal F_{t-1}],\qquad
 Q_T=\sum_{t=1}^TU_t^2. \tag{13}
\]
The Jacobian bounds from the first theorem give
\[
 (KD_1)^{-1}\le\|a\|_2\le h_-^{-1},
 \qquad |U_t|\le L:=\frac{B}{\varepsilon h_-}. \tag{14}
\]
The predictable-QV approximation and terminal covariance nondegeneracy imply
\[
 \frac{A_T^2}{T}
 =a^\top(T^{-1}\langle S\rangle_T)a
 =a^\top\Omega_\infty a+o_P(1),
 \qquad a^\top\Omega_\infty a\ge v_0:=\frac{\omega_-}{(KD_1)^2}>0. \tag{15}
\]
Thus \(A_T^2\to\infty\) in probability uniformly. Equation (3) gives
\[
 \frac{Q_T-A_T^2}{T}
 =a^\top T^{-1}([S]_T-\langle S\rangle_T)a
 =O_P(T^{-1/2}), \tag{16}
\]
so \(Q_T/A_T^2\to_P1\) and \(P(Q_T>0)\to1\) uniformly. With \(\delta=2\), (14)--(15) imply
\[
 A_T^{-4}\sum_{t=1}^TE_P|U_t|^4
 \le A_T^{-4}TL^4\longrightarrow_P0. \tag{17}
\]
Indeed, on \(A_T^2/T\ge v_0/2\), the right side is at most \(4L^4/(Tv_0^2)\), and that event has probability tending uniformly to one.

Every array formed by an arbitrary sequence \(P_T\in\mathfrak P_T\) and unit contrasts \(c_T\) satisfies the hypotheses of \(\mathrm{lem:saco\text{-}self\text{-}normalized\text{-}martingale\text{-}clt}\). Hence
\[
 \frac{a^\top S_T}{\sqrt{a^\top[S]_Ta}}
 =\frac{\sum_{t=1}^TU_t}{\sqrt{Q_T}}\Rightarrow N(0,1). \tag{18}
\]
This convergence is uniform: otherwise a sequence \((P_T,c_T)\) with Kolmogorov distance bounded away from zero would contradict (18) for that triangular array. Weak convergence to continuous \(\Phi\) implies Kolmogorov convergence by partitioning the real line at finitely many continuity points with arbitrarily small intervening \(\Phi\)-increments and using monotonicity between them.

The first theorem gives
\[
 \sqrt T\,c^\top(\widehat\theta_T-\theta^*)
 =-T^{-1/2}a^\top S_T+O_P(e_T). \tag{19}
\]
Equations (3), (7), (12), and \(c^\top V_\infty c=a^\top\Omega_\infty a\) imply
\[
 c^\top\widehat V_Tc-T^{-1}a^\top[S]_Ta=O_P(e_T). \tag{20}
\]
By (15)--(16), both quantities in (20) are at least \(v_0/2\) with probability tending uniformly to one, so all divisions and square roots below are legitimate on that event. Since \(e_T\to0\) and \(|\sqrt x-\sqrt y|=|x-y|/(\sqrt x+\sqrt y)\), equations (18)--(20) yield
\[
 T_T^{\mathrm{rqv}}(c)
 =-\frac{a^\top S_T}{\sqrt{a^\top[S]_Ta}}+o_P(1) \tag{21}
\]
uniformly. The two-sided smoothing inclusions used in the first theorem, together with uniform continuity of \(\Phi\), prove the asserted uniform standard-normal approximation.

Finally, \(\tau=c^\top\theta^*\) and \(\mathrm{def:realized\text{-}qv\text{-}wald\text{-}interval}\) give
\[
 \{\tau\in I_T^{\mathrm{rqv}}(c,\alpha)\}
 =\{|T_T^{\mathrm{rqv}}(c)|\le z_{1-\alpha/2}\}. \tag{22}
\]
The pivotal approximation and \(2\Phi(z_{1-\alpha/2})-1=1-\alpha\) give the stated uniform coverage for every fixed \(\alpha\). No step uses finite support or pointwise convergence of the policy state. The cited Saco theorem supplies the scalar self-normalized martingale implication; equations (1)--(17) are the present primitive verification, and no class-inclusion claim is made.

statements.statement:
Let \(T_\ell\to\infty\) and \(P_\ell\in\mathfrak P_{T_\ell}\) be a sequence along which the law of \(V_\infty\) under \(P_\ell\) converges weakly to a probability law \(\mu\) on the compact covariance set in Theorem 1. Let \(V\sim\mu\). Fix nonzero \(c\) and deterministic positive-definite \(\Sigma\). Then
\[
 \lim_{\ell\to\infty}P_\ell\{\tau\in C_{T_\ell}^{\Sigma}(c,\alpha)\}=1-\alpha
 \quad\text{for every }\alpha\in(0,1)
\]
if and only if
\[
 c^\top Vc=c^\top\Sigma c\qquad\mu\text{-almost surely}.
\]
The necessity identifies the projected variance law of a general centered Gaussian scale mixture from coverage at every nominal level; it makes no claim from validity at only one level.
statements.justification: This theorem exactly characterizes every-level fixed-sandwich validity for one causal contrast under an arbitrary limiting covariance mixing law.
statements.gap: Directional-stability work gives sufficient target-specific conditions and Saco highlights random predictable variance; neither gives the general scale-mixture every-level converse.
statements.consumer: Trial analysts can decide whether a deterministic variance report remains valid for one prespecified HeartSteps excursion-effect contrast even when other covariance directions remain random.
statements.proof_tex:
Set \(s=c^\top\Sigma c>0\) and \(q(v)=c^\top vc\). Positive definiteness of \(\Sigma\), the compact covariance lower bound in Theorem 1, and \(c\ne0\) justify every square root and division below. The deterministic interval definition gives
\[
 \{\tau\in C_{T_\ell}^{\Sigma}(c,\alpha)\}
 =\left\{\left|\sqrt{T_\ell}\,c^\top(\widehat\theta_{T_\ell}-\theta^*)\right|
 \le z_{1-\alpha/2}\sqrt s\right\}. \tag{1}
\]
For a nonunit \(c\), apply Theorem 1 to \(c/\|c\|_2\) and rescale the threshold by \(\|c\|_2\). For fixed \(z>0\), applying its mixture approximation at the two continuity points \(\pm z\sqrt s\) gives
\[
 P_\ell\left\{\left|\sqrt{T_\ell}\,c^\top(\widehat\theta_{T_\ell}-\theta^*)\right|
 \le z\sqrt s\right\}
 =E_{P_\ell}\left[2\Phi\left(z\sqrt{\frac{s}{c^\top V_\infty c}}\right)-1\right]+o(1). \tag{2}
\]
The map \(v\mapsto2\Phi(z\sqrt{s/q(v)})-1\) is bounded and continuous on the compact covariance set. Weak convergence of the laws of \(V_\infty\) therefore turns (2) into
\[
 \int\left\{2\Phi\left(z\sqrt{\frac{s}{q(v)}}\right)-1\right\}\,d\mu(v). \tag{3}
\]
If \(q(V)=s\) \(\mu\)-almost surely, (3) equals \(2\Phi(z)-1\). Taking \(z=z_{1-\alpha/2}\) proves sufficiency at every nominal level.

Conversely, suppose the coverage limit is \(1-\alpha\) for every \(\alpha\in(0,1)\). As \(\alpha\) ranges over \((0,1)\), \(z_{1-\alpha/2}\) ranges over \((0,\infty)\). Equations (1)--(3) imply
\[
 \int\left\{2\Phi\left(z\sqrt{\frac{s}{q(v)}}\right)-1\right\}\,d\mu(v)
 =2\Phi(z)-1\qquad(z>0). \tag{4}
\]
Let \(Q=q(V)\), let \(Z_1\sim N(0,1)\) be independent of \(V\), and put \(X=\sqrt QZ_1\). Both \(X/\sqrt s\) and \(Z_1\) have continuous symmetric laws. Equation (4) equates their absolute-value distribution functions at every positive argument, so symmetry gives equality of their full distribution functions: for \(x\ge0\),
\[
 P(X/\sqrt s\le x)=\{1+P(|X|/\sqrt s\le x)\}/2,
\]
and the negative values follow by reflection.

The compact covariance bounds make \(Q\) bounded. Equality of laws therefore permits comparison of second and fourth moments:
\[
 E[X^2]=E[Q]=s,
 \qquad E[X^4]=3E[Q^2]=3s^2. \tag{5}
\]
Consequently
\[
 E[(Q-s)^2]=E[Q^2]-2sE[Q]+s^2=0. \tag{6}
\]
Thus \(Q=s\) \(\mu\)-almost surely, proving necessity. Requiring every nominal level is precisely what supplies (4) for every \(z>0\); the argument draws no conclusion from a single accidental coverage equality.

statements.statement:
Along any sequence for which the law of \(V_\infty\) converges weakly to \(\mu\), as in Theorem 3, one deterministic positive-definite matrix \(\Sigma\) gives asymptotic coverage \(1-\alpha\) for every \(\alpha\in(0,1)\) and every nonzero contrast \(c\in\mathbb R^d\) if and only if
\[
 V=\Sigma\qquad\mu\text{-almost surely},
\]
where \(V\sim\mu\). Equivalently, the limiting covariance law is the point mass at \(\Sigma\). For a fixed law and horizon-asymptotic sequence, this specializes to \(V_\infty=\Sigma\) almost surely whenever the law of \(V_\infty\) itself is constant across horizons. The implication from all projected equalities to matrix equality uses only finitely many coordinate and pairwise-sum contrasts.
statements.justification: This theorem separates target-specific validity from target-agnostic covariance invariance for an arbitrary limiting covariance law.
statements.gap: Shen and coauthors distinguish directional from matrix stability on the sufficiency side; the general every-level necessity and finite-contrast polarization certificate remain unstated.
statements.consumer: Software reporting many adaptive-experiment contrasts can determine whether one fixed covariance matrix is defensible.
statements.proof_tex:
Suppose first that one deterministic positive-definite \(\Sigma\) gives the asserted coverage for every nonzero \(c\) and every nominal level. Apply Theorem \(\mathrm{thm:contrastwise\text{-}deterministic\text{-}sandwich\text{-}iff}\) to each of the finitely many contrasts
\[
 \mathcal C_0=\{e_r:1\le r\le d\}\cup\{e_r+e_s:1\le r<s\le d\}. \tag{1}
\]
For each \(c\in\mathcal C_0\),
\[
 c^\top(V-\Sigma)c=0\qquad\mu\text{-almost surely}. \tag{2}
\]
Because \(\mathcal C_0\) is finite, the intersection of the probability-one events in (2) still has probability one. On that intersection set \(A=V-\Sigma\), which is symmetric. Taking \(c=e_r\) gives \(A_{rr}=0\). For \(r<s\), taking \(c=e_r+e_s\) and using the diagonal equalities gives
\[
 0=(e_r+e_s)^\top A(e_r+e_s)=2A_{rs}. \tag{3}
\]
Every entry of \(A\) vanishes, so \(V=\Sigma\) \(\mu\)-almost surely.

Conversely, if \(V=\Sigma\) \(\mu\)-almost surely, then \(c^\top Vc=c^\top\Sigma c\) almost surely for every nonzero \(c\). The contrastwise theorem gives coverage \(1-\alpha\) for every such \(c\) and every \(\alpha\in(0,1)\). This proves both directions. The point-mass formulation is exactly almost-sure equality to a deterministic matrix. In the fixed-law special case, taking \(\mu\) to be the common law of \(V_\infty\) gives the stated equivalence with \(V_\infty=\Sigma\) almost surely.

statements.statement: For every \(\varepsilon\in(0,1/6)\), the bounded witness \(P^{\dagger}\) belongs at every \(T\ge2\) to a class \(\mathfrak P_T\) with common choices \(B=2\), \(D_1=D_2=1\), \(h_-=1\), \(L_\Pi=1/12\), \(\omega_-=1\), \(\kappa(u)=u\), \(s_\Theta=1\), \(\rho=\varepsilon/8\), \(r_T=1/(2T)\), and \(\delta_T=0\). Specifically, the policy floor is \(1/6\), \(\sup_{a,\theta}\|g(a,X_t,Y_t(a);\theta)\|_2<2\), the derivative and curvature bounds are \(1\) and \(0\), \(M_{P^{\dagger}}(\theta)=-\theta\), every empirical moment admits an exact minimum of zero in \(\Theta\), and \(T^{-1}\sum_{t=1}^T\|\eta_{t-1}-\bar\eta_J\|_2=1/(2T)\) almost surely. Moreover, \(P^{\dagger}(J=1)=2/5\), \(P^{\dagger}(J=2)=3/5\), so \(\mathcal J=\{1,2\}\); tail selection is exact after the first assignment, \(H=-I_2\), \(\Omega_1=V_1=\operatorname{diag}(1,2)\), and \(\Omega_2=V_2=\operatorname{diag}(1,3)\). Hence for \(\Sigma=\operatorname{diag}(1,2)\) and \(c=(1,0)^\top\), \(c^\top V_jc=c^\top\Sigma c=1\) in both positive-mass basins although \(V_1\ne V_2\), so contrastwise deterministic-sandwich validity holds while matrixwise invariance fails.
statements.justification: This elementary bounded construction verifies inside the stated law class that the contrastwise and matrixwise frontiers are logically distinct.
statements.gap: This is a non-novel existence witness, not evidence about the Guo--Xu recursion; its role is to prevent the directional and matrix claims from being conflated by an unattained free-matrix example.
statements.consumer: Applied analysts can retain a valid primary-endpoint interval in a concrete adaptive experiment without claiming that all secondary contrasts share a stable covariance.
statements.proof_tex:
Fix \(\varepsilon\in(0,1/6)\), \(T\ge2\), and the law \(P^{\dagger}\) of \(\mathrm{def:directional\text{-}matrix\text{-}witness}\). We first verify, one condition at a time, membership in the class of \(\mathrm{def:finite\text{-}attractor\text{-}class}\).

The context is constant, and the two nonzero potential outcomes are independent across occasions and arms with the displayed time-invariant laws. Consequently the full-data vectors \(W_1,\ldots,W_T\) are independent and identically distributed, as required by \(\mathrm{ass:iid\text{-}full\text{-}data}\). At occasion \(t\), the state \(\eta_{t-1}\) is \(\mathcal F_{t-1}\)-measurable and the action is drawn from \(\Pi(\cdot\mid X_t,\eta_{t-1})\) independently of the current potential outcomes. Thus \(\mathrm{ass:sequential\text{-}randomization}\) holds and the logged probability is the probability specified in the construction.

Writing \(u\in[0,1]\) for the state, linear interpolation gives
\[
 \Pi(1\mid x,u)=\frac25,\qquad
 \Pi(2\mid x,u)=\frac14-\frac{u}{12},\qquad
 \Pi(3\mid x,u)=\frac7{20}+\frac{u}{12}.
 \tag{1}
\]
These quantities sum to one. Their coordinatewise minimum over \(u\in[0,1]\) is at least \(1/6\), so (because \(\varepsilon<1/6\)) \(\mathrm{ass:uniform\text{-}overlap}\) holds with the prescribed \(\varepsilon\). Equation (1) also yields, for all \(u,u'\in[0,1]\),
\[
 \sup_{a\in\{1,2,3\}}\left|\Pi(a\mid x,u)-\Pi(a\mid x,u')\right|
 \le \frac1{12}|u-u'|.
 \tag{2}
\]
Hence \(\mathrm{ass:policy\text{-}lipschitz}\) holds with \(L_\Pi=1/12\).

For every \(\theta\in[-1,1]^2\),
\[
 |Y_t(1)-\theta_1|\le1+\sqrt{2/5}<2,
 \qquad
 |Y_t(2)-\theta_2|\le1+\sqrt{1/2}<2.
 \tag{3}
\]
Each nonzero score has only one nonzero coordinate, while the third-arm score is zero. Thus (3) proves \(\mathrm{ass:bounded\text{-}score}\) with the common envelope \(B=2\). The score is affine in \(\theta\) on all of \(\mathbb R^2\), with derivative matrices
\[
 \begin{pmatrix}-1&0\\0&0\end{pmatrix},
 \qquad
 \begin{pmatrix}0&0\\0&-1\end{pmatrix},
 \qquad 0.
\]
Their operator norms are at most one and every second derivative is zero. Therefore \(\mathrm{ass:smooth\text{-}z\text{-}map}\) holds with \(D_1=D_2=1\); the sharp curvature bound is zero, and hence is in particular bounded by the chosen positive envelope \(D_2=1\).

Both Rademacher outcomes have mean zero. By the definition of \(M_{P^{\dagger}}\), summing the three arm-specific mean scores therefore gives
\[
 M_{P^{\dagger}}(\theta)=(-\theta_1,-\theta_2)^\top=-\theta,
 \qquad H=\partial_\theta M_{P^{\dagger}}(0)=-I_2.
 \tag{4}
\]
It follows that \(\theta^*=0\) is the unique root, \(\|M_{P^{\dagger}}(\theta)\|_2=\|\theta\|_2\), and \(\sigma_{\min}(H)=1\). Thus \(\mathrm{ass:uniform\text{-}root\text{-}separation}\) holds with \(\kappa(u)=u\) (with the usual value \(+\infty\) for the infimum over an empty set), and \(\mathrm{ass:jacobian\text{-}nonsingular}\) holds with \(h_-=1\). Moreover,
\[
 \operatorname{dist}(0,\partial[-1,1]^2)=1,
 \tag{5}
\]
so \(\mathrm{ass:root\text{-}interior}\) holds with \(s_\Theta=1\).

For completeness, the empirical moment has an exact zero for every realized assignment and outcome array. For \(a\in\{1,2\}\), put
\[
 W_a=\sum_{t=1}^T\frac{\mathbf 1\{A_t=a\}}{\pi_t(a\mid X_t,\mathcal F_{t-1})}.
\]
All denominators are positive by (1). If \(W_a>0\), define
\[
 \theta_a^{(0)}=
 \frac{\displaystyle\sum_{t=1}^T
 \mathbf 1\{A_t=a\}Y_t(a)/\pi_t(a\mid X_t,\mathcal F_{t-1})}{W_a};
 \tag{6}
\]
if \(W_a=0\), set \(\theta_a^{(0)}=0\). In the first case (6) is a convex combination of values in \([-1,1]\), and in the second case the corresponding empirical coordinate is identically zero. Hence \(\theta^{(0)}=(\theta_1^{(0)},\theta_2^{(0)})^\top\in\Theta\), and direct substitution in the definition of \(G_T\) gives \(G_T(\theta^{(0)})=0\). Since a norm is nonnegative,
\[
 \min_{\theta\in\Theta}\|G_T(\theta)\|_2=0.
 \tag{7}
\]

At the first occasion the state is \(\eta_0=1/2\). By (1), the probability of arm one at that state is \(2/5\). Since \(J=1\) exactly when \(A_1=1\),
\[
 P^{\dagger}(J=1)=\frac25,
 \qquad
 P^{\dagger}(J=2)=\frac35,
 \qquad \mathcal J=\{1,2\}.
 \tag{8}
\]
The random variable \(J\), and hence \(\eta_\infty=\bar\eta_J\), is \(\mathcal F_1\)-measurable and therefore measurable with respect to \(\sigma(\bigcup_{t\ge1}\mathcal F_t)\). This verifies \(\mathrm{ass:finite\text{-}tail\text{-}selection}\). The construction sets \(\eta_s=\bar\eta_J\) for every \(s\ge1\), whereas \(|\eta_0-\bar\eta_J|=1/2\) for either value of \(J\). Consequently
\[
 \frac1T\sum_{t=1}^T|\eta_{t-1}-\eta_\infty|=\frac1{2T}
 \quad\text{almost surely}.
 \tag{9}
\]
Thus \(\mathrm{ass:uniform\text{-}attraction\text{-}modulus}\) holds with \(r_T=1/(2T)\) and \(\delta_T=0\), and
\[
 e_T=T^{-1/2}+\frac1{2T}\longrightarrow0,
 \tag{10}
\]
which verifies \(\mathrm{ass:vanishing\text{-}modulus}\). The proposed radius also obeys the required strict bound because
\[
 0<\rho=\frac{\varepsilon}{8}
 <\min\left\{1,\frac{\varepsilon h_-}{4D_2}\right\}
 =\min\left\{1,\frac{\varepsilon}{4}\right\}.
 \tag{11}
\]

It remains to verify terminal covariance nondegeneracy and compute the promised separation. At \(\theta^*=0\), the arm-specific score outer products are diagonal, the third-arm contribution vanishes, and
\[
 E_{P^{\dagger}}[Y_t(1)^2]=\frac25,
 \qquad
 E_{P^{\dagger}}[Y_t(2)^2]=\frac12.
 \tag{12}
\]
Using (1), (12), and \(\mathrm{def:basin\text{-}covariance}\), evaluation at \(\bar\eta_1=0\) gives
\[
 \Omega_1
 =\operatorname{diag}\left(\frac{2/5}{2/5},\frac{1/2}{1/4}\right)
 =\operatorname{diag}(1,2),
 \tag{13}
\]
whereas evaluation at \(\bar\eta_2=1\) gives
\[
 \Omega_2
 =\operatorname{diag}\left(\frac{2/5}{2/5},\frac{1/2}{1/6}\right)
 =\operatorname{diag}(1,3).
 \tag{14}
\]
By (8), \(\Omega_\infty=\Omega_J\) equals one of (13)--(14) almost surely, and both matrices dominate \(I_2\). Hence \(\mathrm{ass:basin\text{-}nondegeneracy}\) holds with \(\omega_-=1\). Equations (1)--(14) verify every member property in \(\mathrm{def:finite\text{-}attractor\text{-}class}\), with constants and moduli common across horizons. Therefore \(P^{\dagger}\in\mathfrak P_T\) for every \(T\ge2\).

Finally, (4) and the sandwich definition imply
\[
 V_1=H^{-1}\Omega_1H^{-\top}=\operatorname{diag}(1,2),
 \qquad
 V_2=H^{-1}\Omega_2H^{-\top}=\operatorname{diag}(1,3).
 \tag{15}
\]
For \(\Sigma=\operatorname{diag}(1,2)\) and \(c=(1,0)^\top\),
\[
 c^\top V_1c=c^\top V_2c=c^\top\Sigma c=1,
 \qquad V_1\ne V_2.
 \tag{16}
\]
Along any horizon sequence the law of \(V_\infty=V_J\) is the fixed law
\[
 \mu=\frac25\delta_{V_1}+\frac35\delta_{V_2}.
 \tag{17}
\]
The projected equality in (16), together with \(\mathrm{thm:contrastwise\text{-}deterministic\text{-}sandwich\text{-}iff}\), proves asymptotic coverage \(1-\alpha\) for this \(c\), this \(\Sigma\), and every \(\alpha\in(0,1)\). On the other hand, (8), (15), and (17) show that \(V\) is not almost surely constant under \(\mu\). By \(\mathrm{thm:matrixwise\text{-}deterministic\text{-}sandwich\text{-}iff}\), no single deterministic sandwich is valid at every nominal level for every nonzero contrast. This proves the claimed contrastwise--matrixwise separation.

statements.statement:
Consider the bounded-noise Guo--Xu recursion with arbitrary fixed \(\sigma_1,\sigma_2>0\) and deterministic tie arm \(1\). Put \(p=99/100\), \(q=1/100\), and, for \((u,v)\in[q,p]^2\), define
\[
 h(u,v)=\left(\frac{u+16v}{2},\frac{17-u-16v}{2},
                 \frac{u-4v}{4},\frac{-3-u+4v}{24}\right).
\]
For \(t\ge1\), put \(D_{t,a}=\Phi^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,a}\), \(N_{t,a}=b^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,a}\), and \(\Psi_t=(D_{t,1}/t,D_{t,2}/t,N_{t,1}/t,N_{t,2}/t)\). Then \(q^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,a}=O(t^{-1})\) almost surely, \(\Psi_t\) obeys an exact stochastic-approximation recursion with step \(1/(t+1)\), and its affine interpolation is a bounded perturbed solution, hence an asymptotic pseudotrajectory, of the closed convexified inclusion \(\dot\psi\in F(\psi)\) below. Writing \(\Delta(\psi)=n_1/d_1-n_2/d_2\), \(h_+=h(p,q)\), \(h_-=h(q,p)\), \(h_1=h(p,p)\), and \(h_2=h(q,q)\), its graph on \(d_1,d_2>0\) is
\[
 F(\psi)=
 \begin{cases}
  \{h_+-\psi\},&\Delta(\psi)>0,\\
  \{h_--\psi\},&\Delta(\psi)<0,\\
  \operatorname{co}\{h_+,h_-,h_1\}-\psi,&\Delta(\psi)=0,\ d_1<d_2,\\
  \operatorname{co}\{h_+,h_-,h_2\}-\psi,&\Delta(\psi)=0,\ d_1>d_2,\\
  \operatorname{co}\{h_+,h_-,h_1,h_2\}-\psi,&\Delta(\psi)=0,\ d_1=d_2.
 \end{cases}
\]
Every almost-sure normalized-state limit set is internally chain transitive for \(F\) and is contained in the computable parallelogram \(\mathcal C=\{h(u,v):(u,v)\in[q,p]^2\}\); the projected slope limit set is its continuous image under \((d_1,d_2,n_1,n_2)\mapsto(n_1/d_1,n_2/d_2)\).

The smaller inclusion having only \(h_+-\psi\), \(h_--\psi\), and \(\operatorname{co}\{h_+-\psi,h_--\psi\}\) on the switching surface is not a valid unconditional reduction of this recursion. If it were the limiting inclusion, its only internally chain-transitive sets would be the three singletons \(\{h_-\}\), \(\{h(u_0,1-u_0)\}\), and \(\{h_+\}\), where
\[
 u_0=\frac{47+\sqrt{4609}}{150},\qquad
 \frac{N_1}{D_1}=\frac{N_2}{D_2}
 =b_0:=\frac{\sqrt{4609}-91}{1224}
 \quad\text{at }h(u_0,1-u_0).
\]
The correct graph instead has an uncountable family of additional internally chain-transitive singleton equilibria. Explicitly, for
\[
 u\in[u_0,p],\qquad
 v(u)=\frac{3u+18-\sqrt{25u^2-228u+324}}{32},
\]
one has \(h(u,v(u))\in\mathcal C\), equal slope coordinates, first normalized Gram coordinate smaller than the second, and \(0\in F(h(u,v(u)))\). In particular,
\[
 v_*:=v(p)=\frac{2097}{3200}-\frac{3\sqrt{5457}}{640}
\]
gives an equilibrium \(h(p,v_*)\) distinct from \(h_-\), \(h(u_0,1-u_0)\), and \(h_+\). This continuum is an explicit internally-chain-transitive obstruction to a three-candidate conclusion from the standard differential-inclusion route.

For the actual recursion, on \(\mathcal L_+=\{\liminf_t(\widehat\beta^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,1}-\widehat\beta^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,2})>0\}\) and \(\mathcal L_-=\{\limsup_t(\widehat\beta^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,1}-\widehat\beta^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,2})<0\}\), respectively,
\[
 (\widehat\beta^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,1},\widehat\beta^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,2})^\top
 \longrightarrow
 \left(\frac{19}{46},-\frac{79}{3804}\right)^\top
 \quad\text{and}\quad
 \left(-\frac{79}{634},\frac{19}{276}\right)^\top.
\]
Both events have probability bounded away from zero uniformly over \(\eta_0\in\mathsf K_{\mathrm{GX}}\), and the corresponding pathwise Cesaro errors converge to zero. If both slopes have a common-coordinate subsequential limit and \((u,v)\) is a simultaneous subsequential limit of the empirical conditional arm-\(1\) rates, then necessarily
\[
 u^2+12uv-21u-64v^2+72v=0.
\]
The relation \(v=1-u\), and hence the candidate \((u_0,b_0)\), is justified only if same-arm switching-layer occupation is separately excluded; the exact recursion does not provide that exclusion. Consequently, this argument proves neither finite almost-sure tail selection nor zero probability of switching-surface convergence. It also proves no compact-initial-set uniform attraction moduli \(r_T(K_0),\delta_T(K_0)\). These are dynamics-only conclusions: they assert neither membership in \(\mathfrak P_T\) nor applicability of any inference theorem.
statements.justification: The normalized sufficient-statistic recursion gives the strongest rigorous dynamics certificate currently available: it proves the two separated limits and exposes an uncountable switching-equilibrium obstruction in the correct limiting differential inclusion.
statements.gap: The differential-inclusion limit set need not be one of three candidates because the vanishing UCB bonus produces same-arm modes inside the shrinking switching layer. Actual selection within that layer, zero probability of switching convergence, and compact-initial-set uniform attraction still require quantitative escape and equicontinuity estimates not supplied here.
statements.consumer: The result prevents the bounded Guo--Xu analogue from being used as a certified two-basin inference witness while identifying the exact normalized-state graph and the additional dynamics that a future separatrix analysis must control.
statements.proof_tex:
Write \(\mu_1=1/2\), \(\mu_2=1/12\), \(p=99/100\), \(q=1/100\), and \(C_{t,a}=\mathbf 1\{A_t=a\}\).  The recursion in \(\textnormal{def:guoxu-recursion}\) gives, for every \(t\geq 1\),
\[
 D_{t,a}=1+\sum_{s=1}^t C_{s,a}X_s^2,\qquad
 N_{t,a}=\eta_{0,a}+\sum_{s=1}^t C_{s,a}X_s(\mu_a+\sigma_aR_{s,a}),\qquad
 \widehat\beta^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,a}=\frac{N_{t,a}}{D_{t,a}}. \tag{1}
\]
The clipped randomization assigns either arm with conditional probability at least \(q\).  Because \(X_s\) is independent of \(\mathcal F_{s-1}\) and uniform on \(\{-4,1\}\),
\[
 E[C_{s,a}X_s^2\mid\mathcal F_{s-1}]
 \geq qE[X_s^2]=\frac{17}{200}. \tag{2}
\]
We first record the elementary bounded-martingale argument used repeatedly below.  If \((U_s)\) is a scalar martingale-difference sequence with \(|U_s|\leq L\), expansion of the square and iterated conditional expectation make the cross terms zero, so \(E(\sum_{s\leq n}U_s)^2\leq L^2n\).  At \(n=k^2\), the pointwise inequality \(\mathbf 1\{|x|>a\}\leq x^2/a^2\) gives
\[
 P\left(\left|\sum_{s\leq k^2}U_s\right|>\epsilon k^2\right)
 \leq \frac{L^2}{\epsilon^2k^2}.
\]
For every \(K\), the probability that one of these events occurs for some \(k\geq K\) is at most \(L^2\epsilon^{-2}\sum_{k\geq K}k^{-2}\), which tends to zero as \(K\to\infty\).  Thus only finitely many occur almost surely and \(k^{-2}\sum_{s\leq k^2}U_s\to0\).  The at most \(2k+1\) bounded increments between \(k^2\) and \((k+1)^2\) fill the gaps, proving \(n^{-1}\sum_{s\leq n}U_s\to0\) almost surely.

Apply this result to \(C_{s,a}X_s^2-E[C_{s,a}X_s^2\mid\mathcal F_{s-1}]\).  Equations (1)--(2) yield
\[
 \liminf_{t\to\infty}\frac{D_{t,a}}t\geq\frac{17}{200},
 \qquad q^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,a}=D_{t,a}^{-1}=O(t^{-1})
 \quad\text{almost surely}. \tag{3}
\]
The same argument applies to \(C_{s,a}X_sR_{s,a}\): by the ordering in \(\textnormal{def:guoxu-recursion}\), the action is randomized before the reward innovation is observed, and that innovation is conditionally centered.  Hence
\[
 t^{-1}\sum_{s=1}^tC_{s,a}X_sR_{s,a}\longrightarrow0
 \quad\text{almost surely}. \tag{4}
\]
Moreover, (1) expresses each slope as a convex combination of its initial value \(\eta_{0,a}\) and the observed ratios \(Y_s(a)/X_s\), with weights \(1\) and \(C_{s,a}X_s^2\).  The envelope \(M_{\mathrm{GX}}\) therefore bounds both slopes.  Together with bounded \(X_s\) and bounded Rademacher rewards, this bounds every coordinate of \(\Psi_t\); by (3), both normalized Gram coordinates are eventually bounded away from zero.

Define
\[
 U_{t+1}=\bigl(C_{t+1,1}X_{t+1}^2,C_{t+1,2}X_{t+1}^2,
 C_{t+1,1}X_{t+1}Y_{t+1}(1),C_{t+1,2}X_{t+1}Y_{t+1}(2)\bigr).
\]
Dividing the four sufficient-statistic updates by \(t+1\) gives the exact stochastic-approximation recursion
\[
 \Psi_{t+1}-\Psi_t=\frac1{t+1}(U_{t+1}-\Psi_t). \tag{5}
\]
Conditional on \(\mathcal F_t\), let \(u_t\) and \(v_t\) be the arm-one assignment probabilities at contexts \(1\) and \(-4\), respectively.  Conditional centering of the rewards and direct averaging over the two equally likely contexts give
\[
 E[U_{t+1}\mid\mathcal F_t]=h(u_t,v_t), \tag{6}
\]
because the four coordinates on the right are
\[
 \frac{u_t+16v_t}{2},\qquad \frac{17-u_t-16v_t}{2},\qquad
 \mu_1\frac{u_t-4v_t}{2},\qquad
 \mu_2\frac{-3-u_t+4v_t}{2}.
\]
This is precisely the displayed formula for \(h\).

For \(\psi=(d_1,d_2,n_1,n_2)\), put \(\Delta(\psi)=n_1/d_1-n_2/d_2\).  At the current normalized state,
\[
 b_t:=\sqrt{q^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,1}}-\sqrt{q^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,2}}
 =t^{-1/2}\bigl(d_{t,1}^{-1/2}-d_{t,2}^{-1/2}\bigr). \tag{7}
\]
The arm-one minus arm-two UCB index has the sign of \(\Delta(\Psi_t)+b_t\) at context \(1\), and the sign of \(b_t-\Delta(\Psi_t)\) at context \(-4\).  Equation (3) gives \(|b_t|=O(t^{-1/2})\).  Consequently, away from \(\Delta=0\), the two greedy choices are eventually opposite: \((u_t,v_t)=(p,q)\) for \(\Delta>0\), and \((u_t,v_t)=(q,p)\) for \(\Delta<0\).  On \(\Delta=0\), equation (7) has the sign of \(d_2-d_1\).  Thus both contexts make arm one greedy when \(d_1<d_2\), both make arm two greedy when \(d_1>d_2\), and the specified deterministic tie rule makes arm one greedy when \(d_1=d_2\).  The corresponding conditional means are \(h_1,h_2,h_1\), respectively.

This calculation gives the asserted closed convexified graph.  To verify the perturbation condition explicitly, observe that a same-arm mode can occur off the switching surface only if \(|\Delta(\Psi_t)|\leq |b_t|\).  On the eventual compact region already obtained, replace \(n_1\) by \(n_1-d_1\Delta(\Psi_t)\), leaving the other coordinates fixed.  The resulting point lies on \(\Delta=0\) and is within a fixed multiple of \(|\Delta(\Psi_t)|\) of \(\Psi_t\).  Therefore, for a deterministic \(c_0<\infty\) and all sufficiently large \(t\),
\[
 E[U_{t+1}\mid\mathcal F_t]-\Psi_t\in F^{\delta_t}(\Psi_t),
 \qquad \delta_t=c_0t^{-1/2}\longrightarrow0, \tag{8}
\]
where \(F^\delta\) denotes the graph enlargement.  The atoms \(h_+\) and \(h_-\) at every switching point make the graph closed under approach from the two open half-spaces; the atom \(h_1\), respectively \(h_2\), records approach within the switching layer when \(d_1<d_2\), respectively \(d_1>d_2\); and all four atoms at \(d_1=d_2\) close the remaining approaches.  Hence the displayed graph has nonempty compact convex values and is closed.  Its velocities have linear growth because its four atoms are fixed.  Outside a compact convex region containing the eventual trajectory, compose the atom correspondence with metric projection and retain the term \(-\psi\); this supplies a global extension with the same properties without changing the eventual dynamics.

Let \(M_{t+1}=U_{t+1}-E[U_{t+1}\mid\mathcal F_t]\) and \(\gamma_t=1/t\).  Each coordinate is a bounded martingale difference.  Stopping its weighted partial sum at the first crossing of \(\epsilon\) and using orthogonality of the stopped increments gives, for every coordinate and every \(j\),
\[
 P\left\{\sup_{k\geq2^j}\left|\sum_{s=2^j}^k\gamma_{s+1}M_{s+1}\right|>\epsilon\right\}
 \leq \frac{C}{\epsilon^2}\sum_{s=2^j}^{\infty}\gamma_{s+1}^2
 \leq\frac{C'}{\epsilon^22^j}. \tag{9}
\]
The probability that one of the events in (9) occurs for some \(j\geq J\) is at most \(C'\epsilon^{-2}\sum_{j\geq J}2^{-j}\), which tends to zero.  Thus the weighted martingale tails vanish almost surely, uniformly over every bounded interval of stochastic-approximation time.  The increments in (5) are bounded on the eventual compact region, and the mesh \(\gamma_t\) tends to zero, so replacing each discrete state by its affine interpolation adds another graph-enlargement error tending to zero.  Equations (5), (8), and (9), together with boundedness of \(\Psi_t\), verify the bounded-perturbed-solution hypotheses of \(\textnormal{lem:bhs-perturbed-limit-set}\).  That lemma makes the affine interpolation an asymptotic pseudotrajectory and makes its limit set internally chain transitive.

Let
\[
 \mathcal C=h([q,p]^2)=\operatorname{co}\{h_+,h_-,h_1,h_2\}.
\]
Every velocity in \(F(\psi)\) is \(z-\psi\) for some \(z\in\mathcal C\).  If \(P_{\mathcal C}\psi\) is the Euclidean projection and \(V(\psi)=\operatorname{dist}(\psi,\mathcal C)^2\), the projection inequality gives, along every solution and for almost every time outside \(\mathcal C\),
\[
 \frac{d}{ds}V(\psi(s))
 =2(\psi-P_{\mathcal C}\psi)^\top(z-\psi)
 \leq-2\|\psi-P_{\mathcal C}\psi\|_2^2=-2V(\psi). \tag{10}
\]
If a solution starts in \(\mathcal C\), variation of constants writes it as a convex combination of its initial point and a weighted average of points \(z(s)\in\mathcal C\); hence \(\mathcal C\) is positively invariant.  Thus \(V\) is a continuous Lyapunov function for \(\mathcal C\), and \(V(\mathcal C)=\{0\}\) has empty interior.  By \(\textnormal{lem:bhs-lyapunov-ict}\), every internally chain-transitive normalized-state limit set lies in \(\mathcal C\).  Equation (3) keeps \(d_1,d_2\) positive on that limit set, so the slope projection \((d_1,d_2,n_1,n_2)\mapsto(n_1/d_1,n_2/d_2)\) is continuous there.  This proves the first paragraph of the claim.

We next identify exactly what the tempting two-mode inclusion would imply.  Let \(\mathcal C_0=\operatorname{co}\{h_-,h_+\}\) and write its points uniquely as \(h_-+\lambda(h_+-h_-)\), \(0\leq\lambda\leq1\).  Equivalently,
\[
 u=q+(p-q)\lambda,\qquad v=p-(p-q)\lambda=1-u. \tag{11}
\]
Cross-multiplication is legitimate because both Gram coordinates are positive, and direct expansion gives
\[
 \Delta(h(u,v))=0
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 f(u,v):=u^2+12uv-21u-64v^2+72v=0; \tag{12}
\]
indeed, after multiplication by the positive common denominator, the numerator of the slope difference is \(-5f(u,v)\).  Substitution of \(v=1-u\) yields \(f(u,1-u)=-75u^2+47u+8\).  Its unique root in \([q,p]\) is
\[
 u_0=\frac{47+\sqrt{4609}}{150},
\]
and substitution into either slope ratio gives \(b_0=(\sqrt{4609}-91)/1224\).

On \(\mathcal C_0\), the two-mode inclusion reduces to
\[
 \dot\lambda=-\lambda\quad(\lambda<\lambda_0),\qquad
 \dot\lambda=1-\lambda\quad(\lambda>\lambda_0),\qquad
 \dot\lambda\in[-\lambda_0,1-\lambda_0]\quad(\lambda=\lambda_0), \tag{13}
\]
where \(u_0=q+(p-q)\lambda_0\).  Distance squared to \(\mathcal C_0\) first confines every internally chain-transitive set to the segment by the argument of (10).  On the segment, the continuous function
\[
 W(\lambda)=
 \begin{cases}
 \lambda/\lambda_0,&0\leq\lambda\leq\lambda_0,\\
 (1-\lambda)/(1-\lambda_0),&\lambda_0\leq\lambda\leq1
 \end{cases}
\]
strictly decreases along every nonconstant solution outside \(\{0,\lambda_0,1\}\) and never increases from those three points.  Since \(W(\{0,\lambda_0,1\})=\{0,1\}\) has empty interior, \(\textnormal{lem:bhs-lyapunov-ict}\) puts every internally chain-transitive set inside \(\{0,\lambda_0,1\}\) with \(W\) constant.  The set \(\{0,1\}\) is not internally chain transitive: for \(\epsilon<1/3\), the solutions from its endpoints are constant, so no \((\epsilon,S)\)-chain contained in that two-point set can travel from one endpoint to the other.  Thus only the three asserted singletons are internally chain transitive for the smaller inclusion.

That smaller graph cannot approximate the recursion uniformly near the switching surface.  If \(\Delta=0\) and \(d_1<d_2\), equation (7) makes arm one greedy at both contexts and the conditional mean is \(h_1\).  But \(h_1\notin\mathcal C_0\): the affine map \((u,v)\mapsto h(u,v)\) is injective, every parameter pair on \(\mathcal C_0\) satisfies \(u+v=1\), and \(h_1\) corresponds to \((p,p)\), whose sum is \(2p\neq1\).  Compactness therefore gives \(\operatorname{dist}(h_1,\mathcal C_0)>0\).  The \(O(t^{-1/2})\) bonus cannot be discarded uniformly in the \(O(t^{-1/2})\) switching layer.

The extra internally chain-transitive sets of the correct graph are computable.  Solving (12) for its smaller \(v\)-root gives
\[
 v(u)=\frac{3u+18-\sqrt{25u^2-228u+324}}{32}. \tag{14}
\]
For \(u\in[u_0,p]\), substitution verifies \(f(u,v(u))=0\) and \(v(u_0)=1-u_0\).  Direct differentiation gives
\[
 v'(u)=\frac1{32}\left(3+\frac{228-50u}{2\sqrt{25u^2-228u+324}}\right)>0, \tag{15}
\]
because \(u\leq p<1\).  The elementary bounds \(67<\sqrt{4609}<68\) and \(73<\sqrt{5457}<74\) imply
\[
 0.23<v(u_0)<0.24,\qquad 0.308<v(p)<0.314.
\]
Consequently \(q<u,v(u)<p\), \(u+v(u)\geq1\), and
\[
 u+16v(u)\leq p+16v(p)<p+16(0.314)<6.014<\frac{17}{2}. \tag{16}
\]
The first two inequalities put \((u,v(u))\) in the triangle with vertices \((p,q),(q,p),(p,p)\), while (16) says that the first Gram coordinate of \(h(u,v(u))\) is smaller than the second.  Therefore
\[
 h(u,v(u))\in\operatorname{co}\{h_+,h_-,h_1\},\qquad
 \Delta(h(u,v(u)))=0,\qquad 0\in F(h(u,v(u))). \tag{17}
\]
Each singleton in (17) is an equilibrium and hence internally chain transitive.  The map \(h\) is injective because the two linear forms \(u+16v\) and \(u-4v\) have nonzero determinant; the family is therefore uncountable.  At \(u=p\), equation (14) simplifies to
\[
 v(p)=\frac{2097}{3200}-\frac{3\sqrt{5457}}{640}=v_*,
\]
and the bounds above show that this equilibrium differs from the three two-mode candidates.  This proves the stated obstruction.

It remains to separate what the exact recursion itself establishes from what the enlarged inclusion merely permits.  Put \(\Delta_t=\widehat\beta^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,1}-\widehat\beta^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,2}\).  On \(\mathcal L_+\), equation (3) makes the bonus vanish while \(\Delta_t\) is eventually bounded below by a positive constant.  Hence eventually arm one is greedy at context \(1\) and arm two at context \(-4\).  Applying the bounded martingale law proved above to the four context--action counts, and using (4) for the reward noise, gives
\[
 \frac1t(D_{t,1},D_{t,2},N_{t,1},N_{t,2})
 \longrightarrow h_+=\left(\frac{23}{40},\frac{317}{40},\frac{19}{80},-\frac{79}{480}\right). \tag{18}
\]
Equations (1) and (18) yield the first displayed slope limit.  The identical argument on \(\mathcal L_-\) gives
\[
 \frac1t(D_{t,1},D_{t,2},N_{t,1},N_{t,2})
 \longrightarrow h_-=\left(\frac{317}{40},\frac{23}{40},-\frac{79}{80},\frac{19}{480}\right), \tag{19}
\]
and hence the second displayed slope limit.  The limiting slope gaps are, respectively,
\[
 \frac{19}{46}+\frac{79}{3804}=
 \frac{37955}{87492}>0,
 \qquad
 -\frac{79}{634}-\frac{19}{276}=-\frac{16925}{87492}<0. \tag{20}
\]

We now prove the uniform positive-probability assertion rather than infer it from the differential inclusion.  Fix a sufficiently large even \(n\).  For the positive regime, prescribe a length-\(2n\) history consisting first of \(n\) observations with \(X=1,A=1\), then \(n\) observations with \(X=-4,A=2\), and prescribe equally many positive and negative Rademacher signs for each selected arm.  Each prescribed context has probability \(1/2\), each prescribed action has conditional probability at least \(q\), and each prescribed relevant sign has probability \(1/2\).  Thus this history has probability at least \((q/4)^{2n}\), uniformly over \(\eta_0\in[-1,1]^2\).  At its end the slopes are exactly
\[
 \frac{\eta_{0,1}+n/2}{1+n},\qquad
 \frac{\eta_{0,2}-n/3}{1+16n}, \tag{21}
\]
which converge uniformly in \(\eta_0\) to \(1/2\) and \(-1/48\), and both inverse Gram coordinates are \(O(n^{-1})\).

Consider after this prefix the reference policy that makes arm one greedy at context \(1\) and arm two greedy at context \(-4\).  After \(k\) further steps, its conditional-mean sufficient statistics are obtained by adding \(kh_+\) to the four terminal statistics in (21).  Each resulting armwise slope is a denominator-weighted average of its terminal slope and the corresponding ratio in \(h_+\).  By (20)--(21), there are constants \(\gamma_0>0\) and \(n_0<\infty\), independent of \(\eta_0\), such that for \(n\geq n_0\) these two reference slopes differ by at least \(3\gamma_0\) for every \(k\geq0\).  Their Gram coordinates are at least a fixed positive multiple of \(n+k\), so the absolute difference of their UCB bonuses is at most \(C(n+k)^{-1/2}\).  Increasing \(n_0\) makes this bound at most \(\gamma_0\).

Couple the actual rule and this reference rule with the same contexts, rewards, and randomization uniforms, and let \(\zeta\) be the first future occasion at which their greedy maps, computed before that occasion's assignment, disagree for at least one of the two contexts.  Let \(M_k^{(+)}\) be the vector sum of the first \(k\) reference-policy sufficient-statistic increments minus \(kh_+\).  Conditional on the prescribed prefix, \((M_k^{(+)})_{k\geq0}\) is a four-dimensional martingale with a bounded-increment constant depending only on the fixed \(\sigma_1,\sigma_2\).  The martingale maximal inequality and a union bound over the dyadic blocks \(2^jn\leq n+k<2^{j+1}n\) yield, for every fixed \(\gamma>0\),
\[
 P\left(\sup_{k\geq0}\frac{\|M_k^{(+)}\|_\infty}{n+k}>\gamma
 \mathrel{\Big|}\text{the prescribed prefix}\right)
 \leq \sum_{j=0}^{\infty}\frac{C}{\gamma^22^jn}
 =\frac{C_\gamma}{n}. \tag{22}
\]
Indeed, a crossing on the \(j\)-th block requires a partial sum of size at least \(\gamma2^jn\), whereas orthogonality bounds the second moment through the end of that block by a constant times \(2^{j+1}n\), which gives the displayed summand.

Because all reference denominators are bounded below by a constant times \(n+k\), the ratio map is uniformly Lipschitz under the relative perturbation in (22).  Choose \(\gamma\) small enough both to preserve a positive constant lower bound for the perturbed denominators and to change the slope gap by at most \(\gamma_0\).  The same denominator bound makes the reference bonus difference \(O((n+k)^{-1/2})\); enlarge \(n_0\) once more so that it is at most \(\gamma_0\).  On the complementary event in (22), the reference slope gap is therefore at least \(2\gamma_0\), while its bonus difference is at most \(\gamma_0\).  At a putative first exit occasion \(\zeta\), the actual and reference sufficient statistics agree through occasion \(\zeta-1\), so these same bounds apply to the actual pre-assignment state.  Its UCB index difference is consequently positive at context \(1\) and negative at context \(-4\), and the actual greedy map still equals the reference greedy map, a contradiction.  Thus \(\zeta=\infty\) on that event.  Equation (18), now applied under the reference policy, implies \(\mathcal L_+\).  Taking \(n\) still larger so that \(C_\gamma/n\leq1/2\) proves
\[
 \inf_{\eta_0\in\mathsf K_{\mathrm{GX}}}P_{\eta_0}(\mathcal L_+)
 \geq \frac12(q/4)^{2n}>0. \tag{23}
\]
For the negative regime, prescribe first \(n\) observations with \(X=-4,A=1\), then \(n\) with \(X=1,A=2\), again balancing the selected Rademacher signs.  The terminal slopes converge uniformly to \(-1/8\) and \(1/12\); the conditional-mean continuation adds \(kh_-\), and the second strict gap in (20) supplies the same stopped-martingale bootstrap.  Consequently
\[
 \inf_{\eta_0\in\mathsf K_{\mathrm{GX}}}P_{\eta_0}(\mathcal L_-)>0. \tag{24}
\]
On either event the corresponding slope sequence converges.  If \(\beta^+\) and \(\beta^-\) denote the two displayed deterministic limits, split each average at a fixed index after which every summand is at most an arbitrary \(\epsilon>0\); the fixed prefix divided by \(T\) vanishes.  Therefore, respectively,
\[
 \frac1T\sum_{t=1}^T\left\|\bigl(\widehat\beta^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,1},\widehat\beta^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,2}\bigr)^\top-\beta^+\right\|_2\longrightarrow0,
 \qquad
 \frac1T\sum_{t=1}^T\left\|\bigl(\widehat\beta^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,1},\widehat\beta^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,2}\bigr)^\top-\beta^-\right\|_2\longrightarrow0.
\]
This is the asserted pathwise Cesaro-error conclusion.

Finally, define the empirical context-specific arm-one rates
\[
 u_T=\frac2T\sum_{t=1}^T\mathbf1\{X_t=1,A_t=1\},\qquad
 v_T=\frac2T\sum_{t=1}^T\mathbf1\{X_t=-4,A_t=1\}.
\]
The conditional arm-one probability at either context is always in \([q,p]\).  Applying the bounded martingale law to each centered context--action indicator, and to each centered context indicator, shows that every subsequential limit of \((u_T,v_T)\) lies in \([q,p]^2\).  If along a common subsequence both slopes tend to a common coordinate and \((u_T,v_T)\to(u,v)\), then (1), (4), and the context-count law give
\[
 \frac1T(D_{T,1},D_{T,2},N_{T,1},N_{T,2})\longrightarrow h(u,v).
\]
The denominators in this limit are positive because \((u,v)\in[q,p]^2\).  Equality of the two limiting slope ratios is therefore equivalent, by (12), to
\[
 u^2+12uv-21u-64v^2+72v=0.
\]
If same-arm switching-layer occupation is excluded, only the two opposite-context modes remain and (11) forces \(v=1-u\), producing \((u_0,b_0)\).  But (7) and the continuum in (14)--(17) show that this exclusion is not a consequence of the exact recursion or of the differential-inclusion theorem: same-arm modes survive throughout the shrinking switching layer.  The graph is discontinuous there, and the preceding argument supplies neither an avoidance estimate for switching-surface convergence nor a quantitative hitting, escape, or equicontinuity estimate uniform over compact initial sets.  It therefore establishes neither finite almost-sure tail selection nor zero switching-surface probability, and it does not establish compact-uniform moduli \(r_T(K_0),\delta_T(K_0)\).  Since membership in \(\mathfrak P_T\) requires precisely such tail-selection and uniform-attraction properties, no membership or inference conclusion is asserted.  This proves all parts of the theorem.

Let \(p\in[1,\infty)\), \(\gamma>0\), and let \((X_i,\mathcal G_i)_{i=1}^n\) be a scalar martingale-difference sequence with \(n\ge2\) and \(\max_i\|X_i\|_\infty\le\gamma\). Put \(s^2=\sum_{i=1}^nE[X_i^2]\), \(V^2=s^{-2}\sum_{i=1}^nE[X_i^2\mid\mathcal G_{i-1}]\), and \(D=\sup_x|P\{s^{-1}\sum_iX_i\le x\}-\Phi(x)|\). There is a constant \(C_{p,\gamma}\) such that
\[
D\le C_{p,\gamma}\left\{\frac{n\log n}{s^3}+\left(\|V^2-1\|_p^p+s^{-2p}\right)^{1/(2p+1)}\right\}.
\]

Let \((X_{n,t},\mathcal G_{n,t})_{t=1}^{k_n}\) be a scalar martingale-difference array, \(S_n=\sum_tX_{n,t}\), \(Q_n=\sum_tX_{n,t}^2\), and \(A_n^2=\sum_tE[X_{n,t}^2\mid\mathcal G_{n,t-1}]\). If \(A_n^2\to\infty\) in probability, \(P(Q_n>0)\to1\), \(Q_n/A_n^2\to1\) in probability, and for some \(\delta>0\),
\[
 A_n^{-(2+\delta)}\sum_tE[|X_{n,t}|^{2+\delta}]\to0,
\]
then \(S_n/\sqrt{Q_n}\Rightarrow N(0,1)\).

source.verbatim_statement: Theorem A.1 (Self-normalized martingale CLT (Lyapunov form)). Let (xi_{n,t},F_{n,t}) be a martingale difference array with partial sums S_n=sum_{t=1}^{k_n} xi_{n,t}. Define V_n^2=sum E[xi_{n,t}^2|F_{n,t-1}] and Q_n=sum xi_{n,t}^2. Assume: (i) V_n^2 converges in probability to infinity; (ii) P(Q_n>0) tends to 1 and Q_n/V_n^2 converges in probability to 1; and (iii) for some delta>0, V_n^{-(2+delta)} sum E[|xi_{n,t}|^{2+delta}] tends to 0. Then S_n/sqrt(Q_n) converges in distribution to N(0,1).

Under the listed assumptions, S_T/sqrt(Q_T) converges in distribution to N(0,1), and the practical Studentized statistic sqrt(n_eff)(theta_hat-theta_0)/V_hat^{1/2} converges in distribution to N(0,1). Consequently, the Wald interval (4.7) has asymptotically correct coverage at the prespecified horizon, without requiring variance stabilization.

Let \((X_{T,t},\mathcal G_{T,t})_{t=1}^T\) be a scalar martingale-difference triangular array under \(P\), let \(0\le k_T<T\), and suppose \(|X_{T,t}|\le L<\infty\) almost surely. Let \(\lambda_T\) be \(\mathcal G_{T,k_T}\)-measurable and satisfy \(0<v_-\le\lambda_T\le v_+<\infty\) almost surely. If
\[
 \Delta_T:=E_P\left|T^{-1}\sum_{t=k_T+1}^T
 E_P[X_{T,t}^2\mid\mathcal G_{T,t-1}]-\lambda_T\right|\longrightarrow0,
\]
then
\[
 \sup_{z\in\mathbb R}\left|P\left\{T^{-1/2}\sum_{t=k_T+1}^T X_{T,t}\le z\right\}
 -E_P\Phi\left(\frac{z}{\sqrt{\lambda_T}}\right)\right|\longrightarrow0.
\]
The conclusion is uniform over any collection of arrays having common \(L,v_-,v_+\) and a common upper bound on \(\Delta_T\) that tends to zero.
statements.proof_tex:
Put
\[
 Q_T=T^{-1}\sum_{t=k_T+1}^T E_P[X_{T,t}^2\mid\mathcal G_{T,t-1}].
\]
Fix \(\eta>0\) and partition \([v_-,v_+]\) into finitely many Borel intervals \(I_r\) of diameter at most \(\eta\). The events \(B_r=\{\lambda_T\in I_r\}\) belong to \(\mathcal G_{T,k_T}\). Choose \(\lambda_r\in I_r\). For every cell of positive probability, let \(P_r=P(\,\cdot\mid B_r)\). Because \(B_r\in\mathcal G_{T,k_T}\subseteq\mathcal G_{T,t-1}\) for \(t>k_T\), the defining martingale-difference equality remains valid under \(P_r\):
\[
 E_{P_r}[X_{T,t}\mid\mathcal G_{T,t-1}]
 =\frac{E_P[\mathbf 1_{B_r}X_{T,t}\mid\mathcal G_{T,t-1}]}{P(B_r\mid\mathcal G_{T,t-1})}=0.
\]
Here the displayed ratio is read only on \(B_r\), where its denominator is one; equivalently, the equality follows directly by testing against bounded \(\mathcal G_{T,t-1}\)-measurable functions under the conditional law.

Define
\[
 d_r=E_{P_r}|Q_T-\lambda_T|+\eta,
 \qquad q_r=E_{P_r}Q_T,
 \qquad s_r^2=Tq_r.
\]
Since \(|\lambda_T-\lambda_r|\le\eta\) on \(B_r\),
\[
 |q_r-\lambda_r|\le d_r,
 \qquad
 \sum_rP(B_r)d_r\le\Delta_T+\eta.
\]
Call a cell good when \(d_r\le v_-/2\). The total probability of the bad cells is at most \(2(\Delta_T+\eta)/v_-\). On a good cell, \(q_r\ge v_-/2\), and the normalized predictable quadratic variation in the cited Mourrat bound is \(V_r^2=Q_T/q_r\). Therefore
\[
 E_{P_r}|V_r^2-1|
 \le q_r^{-1}E_{P_r}|Q_T-q_r|
 \le \frac{4d_r}{v_-}.
\]
The increments are bounded by \(L\), the number of tail increments is at most \(T\), and \(s_r^2\ge Tv_-/2\). Apply the cited quantitative bound \(\mathrm{lem:mourrat\text{-}bounded\text{-}martingale\text{-}clt}\) with \(p=1\) under \(P_r\). It gives a common constant \(C\) such that
\[
 \sup_z\left|P_r\left\{T^{-1/2}\sum_{t>k_T}X_{T,t}\le z\right\}
 -\Phi\left(\frac z{\sqrt{q_r}}\right)\right|
 \le C\left\{\frac{\log T}{\sqrt T}+\left(d_r+T^{-1}\right)^{1/3}\right\}
\]
on every good cell. The normal scale family is uniformly Lipschitz in its variance on \([v_-/2,2v_+]\): indeed, with \(\phi\) the standard normal density,
\[
 \sup_z\left|\frac{\partial}{\partial q}\Phi\left(\frac z{\sqrt q}\right)\right|
 =\sup_u\frac{|u|\phi(u)}{2q}\le C_{v_-}.
\]
Consequently, on a good cell,
\[
 \sup_z\left|\Phi\left(\frac z{\sqrt{q_r}}\right)
 -E_{P_r}\Phi\left(\frac z{\sqrt{\lambda_T}}\right)\right|
 \le C_{v_-}d_r.
\]
After multiplying by \(P(B_r)\), summing, bounding each bad-cell discrepancy by one, and using concavity of \(x^{1/3}\), we obtain
\[
 \sup_z\left|P\left\{T^{-1/2}\sum_{t>k_T}X_{T,t}\le z\right\}
 -E_P\Phi\left(\frac z{\sqrt{\lambda_T}}\right)\right|
 \le C\left\{\frac{\log T}{\sqrt T}+\left(\Delta_T+\eta+T^{-1}\right)^{1/3}
 +\Delta_T+\eta\right\}.
\]
Taking, for example, \(\eta=T^{-1}\) proves the assertion. Every constant in the display depends only on \(L,v_-,v_+\), which also proves the stated uniformity.
